lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Scan Existing Solutions & Technology" (Discover → Research Solution Options) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Know every way the problem is already solved before considering building it.
Done looks like: A technology scan: products, open-source libraries, platform features and 'do nothing', each with fit, maturity, licence and cost band — and a shortlist.

I'll attach or paste: Technical problem statement; Technical constraint log.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. List candidate solutions → Technology scan
   List the existing ways to solve my technical problem statement: commercial products, open-source libraries, features of platforms the client already has, improving what's there, and doing nothing.
2. Check fit against problem & constraints → Technology scan
   Check each candidate against my hard constraints (data region, interfaces, auth) and the problem statement, and mark fits yes / no / unknown with the reason.
3. Check maturity, licence & cost → Technology scan
   For each candidate that fits, record maturity, licence and cost band, with sources. Flag any licence that needs legal review.
4. Shortlist agreed? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)
   Propose a shortlist of two or three genuinely different routes plus 'do nothing', with why each made it.

Produce: Technology scan. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Before you finish, check it against: Every candidate has fit, maturity, licence and cost band; 'Do nothing' included; Fit, maturity, licence, cost per candidate; Do nothing included.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

decisions: Which options really meet the targets?

lessons.title: Prototype the Riskiest Unknowns
lessons.summary: Build the smallest throwaway prototype that proves or kills the riskiest assumption.

definition.purpose: Turn the riskiest remaining unknown into evidence by building the smallest thing that could prove it wrong.
definition.outcome: Spike results for each planned spike: question, approach, result with data, remaining unknowns and what it changes.
definition.jtbd: Help me know — not hope — that the risky part works before anyone commits to it.
exit: Each spike answered within its timebox
Results read against the success signal set in advance

normal: Pick the riskiest unknown from the matrix and spike plan
Run it on realistic, masked data
Read the result against the success signal

cases.happyPath: The prototype meets its success signal inside the timebox.
alternates: Result is borderline → state it plainly; don't move the signal
edgeCases: Timebox runs out → record what's known and what isn't
exceptions: Prototype disproves the favourite → good: it saved the build
failures: The prototype can't be built at all

routing.alternate: Answer found in docs mid-spike → stop early and record it
routing.escalation: Needs more time or money → tech lead
routing.stop: Every option fails → back to framing — recorded in the learning log

principles: Learn the most for the least

decisions: Does the risky part actually work?

agents: AI coding agent for building the prototype
execution.authority: Tech lead reads the verdict; extending a timebox needs the tech lead.

traceability: Spike results close H-## via SPK-##
learning: Spikes that changed the plan — learning log
